fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Investigates employment discrimination under NRS ch. 613.

discriminationDeadline.detail: An employment complaint must be filed with NERC within 300 days of the alleged practice. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Written notice must be given to the employer as soon as practicable, but within 7 days after the accident.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: A claim for compensation must be filed with the insurer within 90 days after the accident.

wcAgency.value: Nevada Division of Industrial Relations, Workers' Compensation Section
wcAgency.detail: Regulates insurers and claims; appeals go to the Department of Administration hearings division.

minimumWage.detail: No change on Jan 1, 2027: the state's inflation off-ramp was triggered, per NYDOL as reported by trackers.

tippedWage.detail: Cash wage for tipped food service workers in 2026, with tip credits of $5.65 and $5.30.

fairEmploymentAgency.value: New York State Division of Human Rights
fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Investigates employment discrimination under the NY Human Rights Law.

discriminationDeadline.detail: A complaint must be filed within 3 years of the discriminatory act. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Written notice must be given to the employer within 30 days after the accident.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: A claim must be filed within 2 years after the accident (or date of disablement for occupational disease).

wcAgency.value: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
wcAgency.detail: State board that receives claims and decides disputes.

minimumWage.detail: For employers with gross receipts over $405,000; rises to $11.40 on Jan 1, 2027 (small-employer threshold rises to $419,000).

tippedWage.detail: Cash wage for larger employers; rises to $5.70 on Jan 1, 2027.

fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Investigates employment discrimination under R.C. ch. 4112.

discriminationDeadline.detail: A charge must be filed with the Commission within 2 years of the discriminatory practice. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: Claims are barred unless notice of the injured body parts reaches BWC or the Industrial Commission within 1 year of injury.

wcAgency.value: Ohio Bureau of Workers' Compensation (and Industrial Commission of Ohio)
wcAgency.detail: BWC handles claims; the Industrial Commission hears disputed claims.

minimumWage.detail: Applies to employers with 10+ full-time workers or over $100,000 in sales; others may pay $2.00 if not FLSA-covered. No 2027 change.

tippedWage.detail: DOL lists the federal $2.13 cash wage; non-FLSA employers may take up to a 50% tip credit under state law.

fairEmploymentAgency.value: Oklahoma Attorney General, Office of Civil Rights Enforcement
fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Takes employment discrimination complaints under the Oklahoma Anti-Discrimination Act.

discriminationDeadline.detail: Complaints must be filed within 180 days of the last unlawful employment practice. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

minimumWage.detail: $16.80 Portland metro, $14.55 nonurban counties, July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027; next adjustment is July 1, 2027.

tippedWage.detail: Oregon bans tip credits; tipped workers get the full regional minimum wage before tips.

fairEmploymentAgency.value: Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries (BOLI), Civil Rights Division
fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Takes employment discrimination complaints under ORS ch. 659A.

discriminationDeadline.detail: Complaints under ORS 659A.030, .082 and .112 may be filed up to 5 years after the act; most other complaints within 1 year. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Notify the employer immediately, and no later than 90 days after the accident (up to 1 year with good cause or employer knowledge).

wcClaimDeadline.detail: In Oregon the notice of accident is the claim; a late claim may be accepted up to 1 year after the accident in limited cases.

wcAgency.value: Oregon Workers' Compensation Division (Dept. of Consumer and Business Services)
wcAgency.detail: Oversees claims; disputes go to the Workers' Compensation Board.

minimumWage.detail: Pennsylvania's minimum equals the federal rate; no increase scheduled for Jan 1, 2027.

tippedWage.detail: Employers may take up to a $4.42/hour tip credit against the $7.25 minimum.

fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Investigates employment discrimination under the PA Human Relations Act.

discriminationDeadline.detail: A PHRC complaint must be filed within 180 days of the alleged discrimination. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Benefits start only after notice; notice within 21 days preserves full benefits, and no compensation is due without notice within 120 days.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: Claims are barred unless compensation is agreed or a claim petition is filed within 3 years of the injury.

wcAgency.value: Pennsylvania Bureau of Workers' Compensation (Dept. of Labor & Industry)
wcAgency.detail: Administers the system; workers' comp judges decide claim petitions.

minimumWage.detail: Rises to $17.00 on Jan 1, 2027 under state law.

tippedWage.detail: Employers may take up to a $12.11/hour tip credit; the employer must make up any shortfall.

fairEmploymentAgency.value: Rhode Island Commission for Human Rights
fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Investigates employment discrimination under the RI Fair Employment Practices Act.

discriminationDeadline.detail: A charge must be filed within 1 year of the unlawful employment practice. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Notice of injury must be given to the employer within 30 days after it happens or appears.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: A claim is barred unless weekly payments started or a petition was filed within 2 years of the injury.

wcAgency.value: RI Dept. of Labor and Training, Division of Workers' Compensation (and Workers' Compensation Court)
wcAgency.detail: DLT administers the system; petitions are decided by the RI Workers' Compensation Court.

minimumWage.detail: No state minimum wage law; the federal $7.25 applies. No increase is scheduled for Jan 1, 2027.

tippedWage.detail: Employers may count up to $5.12/hour in tips toward the $7.25 federal minimum; if tips fall short, the employer must make up the difference.
tippedWage.cite: 29 U.S.C. § 203(m); U.S. DOL tipped wage table

fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Investigates employment discrimination under the SC Human Affairs Law.

discriminationDeadline.detail: A complaint must be filed within 180 days of the discriminatory practice. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Notify the employer immediately; no compensation is payable unless notice is given within 90 days of the accident.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: A claim must be filed with the Commission within 2 years of the accident.

wcAgency.value: South Carolina Workers' Compensation Commission
wcAgency.detail: State commission that receives claims and decides disputes.

minimumWage.detail: Indexed each Jan 1; rises to $12.30 on Jan 1, 2027.

tippedWage.detail: Tipped cash wage is half the minimum; rises to $6.15 on Jan 1, 2027.

fairEmploymentAgency.value: South Dakota Division of Human Rights
fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Part of the Dept. of Labor & Regulation; investigates employment discrimination.

discriminationDeadline.detail: A charge must be filed within 180 days after the discriminatory practice. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Written notice must be given to the employer no later than 3 business days after the injury.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: A petition for hearing must be filed within 2 years after the insurer notifies the worker in writing that it is denying the claim.

wcAgency.value: South Dakota Dept. of Labor & Regulation, Division of Labor and Management
wcAgency.detail: Administers workers' comp claims and hearings.

minimumWage.detail: No state minimum wage law; the federal $7.25 applies. No increase is scheduled for Jan 1, 2027.

tippedWage.detail: Employers may count up to $5.12/hour in tips toward the $7.25 federal minimum; if tips fall short, the employer must make up the difference.
tippedWage.cite: 29 U.S.C. § 203(m); U.S. DOL tipped wage table

discriminationDeadline.detail: The EEOC lists a 180-day state agency deadline in Tennessee. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Written notice must be given to the employer within 15 days of the accident unless the delay is excused.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: A petition for benefit determination must be filed within 1 year of the accident (if no benefits were paid).

wcAgency.value: Tennessee Bureau of Workers' Compensation
wcAgency.detail: Part of the Dept. of Labor and Workforce Development; administers claims and the Court of Workers' Compensation Claims.

minimumWage.detail: Texas adopts the federal rate by reference; no increase scheduled for Jan 1, 2027.

tippedWage.detail: Employers may count up to $5.12/hour in tips toward the $7.25 federal minimum; if tips fall short, the employer must make up the difference.

fairEmploymentAgency.value: Texas Workforce Commission, Civil Rights Division
fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Takes employment discrimination complaints under Texas Labor Code ch. 21.

discriminationDeadline.detail: A complaint must be filed within 180 days (300 days for sexual harassment). Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Notify the employer no later than the 30th day after the injury (or after learning an occupational disease may be work-related).

wcClaimDeadline.detail: A claim must be filed with the Division no later than 1 year after the injury.

wcAgency.value: Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation
wcAgency.detail: Regulates the system and resolves disputes.

minimumWage.detail: Utah's minimum equals the federal rate; no increase scheduled for Jan 1, 2027.

tippedWage.detail: Employers may count up to $5.12/hour in tips toward the $7.25 federal minimum; if tips fall short, the employer must make up the difference.

fairEmploymentAgency.value: Utah Antidiscrimination and Labor Division (Labor Commission)
fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Takes employment discrimination complaints under the Utah Antidiscrimination Act.

discriminationDeadline.detail: A request for agency action must be filed within 180 days of the discriminatory practice. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Notify the employer (or division) within 180 days of the injury or the claim is barred.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: An application for hearing must be filed with the Adjudication Division within 6 years of the accident.

wcAgency.value: Utah Labor Commission, Industrial Accidents Division
wcAgency.detail: Oversees claims; the Adjudication Division hears disputes.

minimumWage.detail: Under 2026 HB1/SB1, rises to $13.75 on Jan 1, 2027 and $15.00 on Jan 1, 2028, then indexed from 2029.

tippedWage.detail: Employers may take up to a $10.64/hour tip credit against the $12.77 minimum.

fairEmploymentAgency.value: Virginia Office of the Attorney General, Office of Civil Rights
fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Takes discrimination complaints under the Virginia Human Rights Act.

discriminationDeadline.detail: A complaint must be filed with the Office of Civil Rights within 2 years. File with EEOC within 300 days to keep federal claims.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Written notice must be given to the employer within 30 days of the accident unless reasonably excused.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: The right to compensation is barred unless a claim is filed with the Commission within 2 years of the accident.

wcAgency.value: Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission
wcAgency.detail: State commission that receives claims and decides disputes.

minimumWage.detail: Indexed each Jan 1; the 2027 rate had not been announced as of mid-October 2026.

tippedWage.detail: Service or tipped employees get half the minimum wage as a cash wage.

fairEmploymentAgency.value: Vermont Attorney General's Office, Civil Rights Unit
fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Enforces Vermont's Fair Employment Practices Act for private employers.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Notice of the injury must be given to the employer as soon as practicable.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: A claim should be made within 6 months of injury; late claims are excused in some cases, but no claim may start after 3 years.

wcAgency.value: Vermont Department of Labor, Workers' Compensation Division
wcAgency.detail: Administers claims and hearings.

minimumWage.detail: Indexed each Jan 1; rises to $17.73 on Jan 1, 2027. Seattle and other cities set higher rates.

tippedWage.detail: Washington bans tip credits; tipped workers get the full minimum wage before tips.

fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Investigates employment discrimination under the Washington Law Against Discrimination.

discriminationDeadline.detail: An employment complaint must be filed within 6 months of the discriminatory act. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Report the accident to your employer or supervisor right away; the statute sets no number of days.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: A claim must be filed within 1 year after the injury (2 years for occupational disease under RCW 51.28.055).

wcAgency.value: Washington Department of Labor & Industries (L&I)
wcAgency.detail: Runs the state workers' comp fund and handles claims.

minimumWage.detail: Wisconsin's minimum equals the federal rate; no increase scheduled for Jan 1, 2027.
minimumWage.cite: Wis. Stat. § 104.035; Wis. Admin. Code DWD § 272.03

tippedWage.detail: Employers may take up to a $4.92/hour tip credit against the $7.25 minimum.

fairEmploymentAgency.value: Wisconsin Equal Rights Division (Dept. of Workforce Development)
fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Investigates employment discrimination under the Wisconsin Fair Employment Act.

discriminationDeadline.detail: A complaint must be filed with the department within 300 days of the alleged discrimination. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: The employer must receive actual notice within 30 days of the injury (or of learning it is work-related).

wcClaimDeadline.detail: If no compensation was paid, an application must be filed within 2 years; otherwise a 6-year limit applies to traumatic injuries.

wcAgency.value: Wisconsin Dept. of Workforce Development, Worker's Compensation Division
wcAgency.detail: Administers claims and hearings.

minimumWage.detail: Applies to employers with 6+ employees at one location; no increase scheduled for Jan 1, 2027.

tippedWage.detail: Employers may count tips for up to 70% of the minimum wage ($6.13/hour).

fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Now housed in the Office of Inspector General; investigates employment discrimination.

discriminationDeadline.detail: A complaint must be filed within 365 days of the most recent act of discrimination. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.
discriminationDeadline.cite: W. Va. Human Rights Act (as amended 2024)

wcClaimDeadline.detail: The claim application must be filed within 6 months of the injury, or the right to compensation is forever barred.

wcAgency.value: West Virginia Offices of the Insurance Commissioner (Workers' Compensation)
wcAgency.detail: Regulates the private workers' comp market; claims go to the employer's carrier.

minimumWage.detail: Wyoming's own minimum is $5.15, but the federal $7.25 applies to FLSA-covered employers. No Jan 1, 2027 change.

tippedWage.detail: Employers may count up to $5.12/hour in tips toward the $7.25 federal minimum; if tips fall short, the employer must make up the difference.

fairEmploymentAgency.value: Wyoming Dept. of Workforce Services, Labor Standards Office (Fair Employment Program)
fairEmploymentAgency.detail: Investigates employment discrimination under the Wyoming Fair Employment Practices Act.

discriminationDeadline.detail: A verified complaint must be filed with the department within 6 months of the violation. Dual-filing with the state agency extends the federal EEOC deadline to 300 days.

wcInjuryNotice.detail: Report the injury to the employer as soon as practical, no later than 72 hours; a formal injury report is due within 10 days.

wcClaimDeadline.detail: A claim for benefits must be filed within 1 year after the injury (or its discovery).

wcAgency.value: Wyoming Dept. of Workforce Services, Workers' Compensation Division
wcAgency.detail: Runs Wyoming's exclusive state workers' comp fund and handles claims.
